The setup is a quantized Qwen3.6-27B GPTQ model on 2 GPUs in one host without NVLink. You want the pros and cons, and any known bugs of LMCache with Qwen3.6-27B. I will also check the premises: that the model exists, that this GPU topology is sensible, and that GPTQ and LMCache work together.Two results look directly relevant: LMCache #4247, which reports silent output corruption on Qwen3.6-27B, and vLLM #45407, a crash. They look directly relevant, so I'll check their status and details.# LMCache with vLLM for Qwen3.6-27B GPTQ-Pro on 2 GPUs without NVLink

## Verdict

**I would not use LMCache as a default for this setup today.** It only pays off for specific workloads, and it carries a real risk of silent output corruption on this model class.

It is worth a trial only if at least one of these holds:
- Many long sessions share prefixes and overflow vLLM's in-GPU prefix cache.
- You need the cache to survive restarts.
- You want two vLLM replicas to share one cache.

Otherwise start with vLLM's native prefix caching. Qwen3.6-27B can be served by LMCache, but not in the configuration you describe.

## What I challenged in your question

1. **"2 GPUs" may not be needed, and TP=2 may be the wrong topology.**
   - vLLM's documentation says that without NVLink you should use pipeline parallelism rather than tensor parallelism "for higher throughput and lower communication overhead" ([vLLM parallelism docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/serving/parallelism_scaling/)).
   - The vLLM recipe lists Int4 Qwen3.6-27B as fitting "single 24 GB GPU" ([recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B)).
   - The alternative is two independent replicas, one per GPU. That depends on your VRAM, which you did not state.
   - Pipeline parallelism has its own problems here. A Reddit report says pipeline parallelism plus MTP does not work for this model; I only saw the search snippet, so treat it as unconfirmed. vLLM #49355, MTP broken with PP>1, is open but concerns a different model.
   - LMCache PR #4082, which adds pipeline-parallel support in multi-server mode, is closed and unmerged ([vLLM #48236](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48236), GitHub API). LMCache plus PP is therefore unverified.
   - TP=2 over PCIe is not broken. The checkpoint's own card reports about 64 tok/s on 2x RTX 3090 with TP=2 and `--disable-custom-all-reduce` ([HF card](https://huggingface.co/groxaxo/Qwen3.6-27B-GPTQ-Pro-4bit)). Pipeline parallelism gives no single-stream latency gain.
2. **LMCache's validation does not cover your configuration.** LMCache's recipe validates `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` on **1 GPU** only. GPTQ weights, TP=2 and image KV are not listed, and the page says caching of image/video KV is "not validated" ([LMCache recipe](https://docs.lmcache.ai/recipes/qwen3_5.html)). The "Pro" checkpoint is a community quant (groxaxo, FOEM method), not an official Qwen release.
3. **Qwen3.6-27B is a hybrid model.** It has 48 Gated-DeltaNet layers and only 16 full-attention layers ([config.json](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B/raw/main/config.json)). This is why LMCache here is far more fragile than on Llama-style models.
4. **I assumed "LLM Cache" means LMCache.** Say so if you meant something else.

## Pros

- **TTFT on a cache miss.** 100k-token cold prefill takes about 101 s on 2x 3090 ([noonghunna/qwen36-dual-3090](https://github.com/noonghunna/qwen36-dual-3090)). Restoring from host RAM could cut that sharply, but I found no published Qwen3.6 restore benchmark.
- **A larger cache tier.** The cache lives in host RAM or on disk and persists across restarts.
- **Sharing between replicas.** One LMCache server per node can serve several vLLM instances ([LMCache MP overview](https://docs.lmcache.ai/mp/index.html)). This is the strongest fit if you run two single-GPU replicas.
- **Now officially supported.** Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 are documented and have a CI correctness gate.

## Cons and known bugs

All versions below are as of LMCache v0.5.7 (2026-11-05) and vLLM stable v0.32.0 (2026-10-18).

| Issue | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Silent token-salad corruption on any shared-prefix hit. Cause: a layout change in vLLM 0.26 on the FlashInfer backend. | Fixed by LMCache #4253, merged 2026-09-28. GitHub compare shows v0.5.6 and v0.5.7 contain it. | [#4247](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4247) |
| Multi-step retrieve corruption with MTP | Closed 2026-09-23 | [#4984](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4984) |
| Mixed local plus external hit makes MTP5 degenerate, with draft acceptance at exactly 0 | **Open** | [#5675](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5675) |
| Hybrid persistence stores 1 of N kernel pages on vLLM 0.26 or later | **Open**. The root cause looks like the #4247 one, but I did not confirm it is fixed. | [#4701](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4701) |
| Failed batched L1 allocation commits a torn TP prefix, so retrieve silently returns corrupt KV | **Open**. TP-relevant. | [#5344](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5344) (title only) |
| Recurrent-state restore under speculative decoding | **Open** | [#6251](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/6251) |
| Max concurrency fell from 130 to 40 with LMCache on TP2 Qwen3.6-27B-FP8. A lower `--max-num-batched-tokens` was needed to avoid CUDA OOM. | **Open**, cause unconfirmed | [#4514](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4514) |
| TP=2 needs `--max-workers` of at least 2. Otherwise you get 0% external hits and a false clean result. | Third-party report | [#4247 thread](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4247) |
| Security CVEs: MP-mode pickle (fixed in 0.5.6) and multimodal hash collision (fixed in 0.5.5) | Fixed | [v0.5.6 notes](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/releases/tag/v0.5.6), [#4086](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4086) |

Two caveats come with the open issues:
- Generation is not bit-exact between cached and fresh runs. GDN backends do not support batch-invariant mode, so validate at score level, not token level ([hybrid docs](https://docs.lmcache.ai/mp/hybrid_models.html)).
- vLLM's own Mamba prefix caching in `align` mode is marked experimental upstream.

Cost per cached token is also high. This is my inference from config.json and the hybrid docs:
- Full-attention KV is about 64 KiB per token at fp16 (16 layers × 2 × 4 KV heads × 256 head dim × 2 bytes).
- Each chunk also stores a recurrent state of roughly 150 MB. A third-party comment independently quotes about 150 MB per entry.
- That is about 250 KB per token, or roughly 25 GB of host RAM per 100k-token context, several times a plain-attention model.

## Alternatives

| Option | Wins when |
|---|---|
| vLLM native prefix caching only (`--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`) | One user or agent, with a working set that fits in GPU memory. This is the lowest-risk baseline. |
| Two single-GPU replicas behind a router, if the quant plus KV fits in 24 GB | Throughput matters and PCIe all-reduce is the bottleneck. Pair with LMCache only if you need shared or persistent cache. |
| TP=2, as on the model card | Single-stream latency, or long context that does not fit on one GPU. |
| Pipeline parallelism (vLLM's no-NVLink advice) | Aggregate throughput. Test MTP and LMCache compatibility first. |
| vLLM `OffloadingConnector` | You want CPU offload without a second process. I could not verify Qwen3.6 hybrid support. Issue #36463 (Qwen3.5-27B failing to start with CPU offload) is only a search snippet. |
| Official `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-GPTQ-Int4` instead of the community quant | You want a checkpoint closer to what LMCache and vLLM CI exercise. |

Also note vLLM issue #45238, open: hybrid prefix-cache reuse depends on block-size geometry. One reporter measured 25-54% hit rates on a small model even without LMCache, and the issue is partly mitigated on main. Check your own native hit rate before assuming a gap that LMCache must fill.

## Recommendation

1. **Measure the native baseline first.** Run vLLM alone and track `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` over `vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total`, plus TTFT on your real prompts. If hit rate is high and sessions fit in GPU memory, stop here.
2. **If you try LMCache, pin versions.** Use LMCache 0.5.7 or later and a vLLM release that LMCache's compatibility page lets you validate. LMCache's own page says a newer vLLM is unvalidated until you test it ([compatibility](https://docs.lmcache.ai/getting_started/compatibility.html)). Follow the documented setup:
   - Set `--mamba-cache-mode align` and `--enable-prefix-caching`.
   - Run the server with `--separate-object-groups`. Do not pass `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`.
   - Set `kv_connector_module_path` to `lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector`.
   - Set `--max-workers` to at least the TP size.
3. **Start conservative.** Use no MTP, TP=1 or a single replica first, and no fp8 KV. On Ampere, fp8 KV forces FlashInfer, the backend hit by #4247 ([#4886](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4886)).
4. **Validate before trusting it.** Check these in order:
   - The startup log shows `KV cache group edits applied` with `subpaged-attention-view` if you use FlashInfer.
   - "External prefix cache hit rate" is non-zero.
   - Follow the documented store, `reset_prefix_cache`, re-run cycle (needs `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`) with a gsm8k score comparison. Wait about 30 s after the store before resending.
   - Run the reproducer from #4247 as a garbage detector.
   - Compare max concurrency and TTFT (cold, GPU-warm, LMCache-warm) against the baseline.
5. **Treat any non-zero garbage count as a stop condition.**

Confidence: medium. The bug catalogue is well sourced, but I do not know your GPU model, VRAM, host RAM, context lengths or session count. The question that would most change this recommendation is whether the 4-bit model plus KV fits on a single GPU for your context length, which would favour two replicas.

Arkane Cloud est un fournisseur réel, avec une offre technique crédible et des prix compétitifs. Les preuves publiques de solidité sont faibles. Understood: you want to know how KServe serves models with vLLM, how multiple GPUs are handled (tensor, data or pipeline parallelism), and how vLLM options are passed and handled. I'll treat this as a standard research question, with a check of the KServe docs.# KServe + vLLM: architecture, multi-GPU parallelism and option handling

All claims below come from the KServe 0.20 docs and the vLLM stable docs, which I fetched for this answer. Where a point is my inference rather than the docs, I say so.

## 1. How KServe and vLLM fit together

KServe is the Kubernetes control plane. vLLM is the inference engine running inside the pod. There are two ways to deploy it.

**A. `InferenceService` with the Hugging Face runtime (the classic path).**
- KServe ships a "Hugging Face serving runtime" that uses vLLM as its backend engine. Its OpenAI-compatible endpoints are `openai/v1/completions`, `openai/v1/chat/completions`, `openai/v1/embeddings` and `openai/v1/rerank`.
- If vLLM does not support the model, KServe falls back to the plain Hugging Face backend.
- KServe picks the CUDA image automatically if you request `nvidia.com/gpu`, and the CPU image otherwise.
- Source: https://kserve.github.io/website/docs/model-serving/generative-inference/overview

**B. `LLMInferenceService` (newer, GenAI-specific, API version `v1alpha1`).**
- It is built on llm-d. You supply the vLLM container yourself, for example `vllm/vllm-openai`.
- It adds Gateway API routing and an inference-aware scheduler. The scheduler is KV-cache aware.
- It also supports prefill/decode disaggregation, multi-node serving with LeaderWorkerSet, and LoRA adapters.
- The KServe docs say `InferenceService` can still serve LLMs, but "only for basic single-node deployments".
- Source: https://kserve.github.io/website/docs/model-serving/generative-inference/llmisvc/llmisvc-overview

## 2. How multiple GPUs and parallelism are handled

KServe does not implement parallelism itself. It translates its CRD fields into vLLM's own parallelism flags, and vLLM then splits the model across GPUs. Which strategies you get depends on which CRD you use.

| Strategy | `InferenceService` (HF runtime) | `LLMInferenceService` |
|---|---|---|
| Tensor parallel (TP) | Yes: `workerSpec.tensorParallelSize` | Yes: `spec.parallelism.tensor` |
| Pipeline parallel (PP) | Yes: `workerSpec.pipelineParallelSize` | Not listed in `spec.parallelism` |
| Data parallel (DP) | No (use replicas and autoscaling) | Yes: `data` and `dataLocal` |
| Expert parallel (EP, for MoE models) | No | Yes: `expert: true` |

### `InferenceService` with multi-node

Source: https://kserve.github.io/website/docs/model-serving/generative-inference/multi-node

- You use the `kserve-huggingfaceserver-multinode` runtime and set `workerSpec` on the InferenceService. Without `workerSpec`, multi-node is not enabled.
- KServe starts one head pod plus worker pods, which form a Ray cluster. Each pod requests GPUs.
- The docs give the arithmetic: `Total GPUs = tensorParallelSize × pipelineParallelSize`.
- Example: TP=8 and PP=2 on 2 nodes with 8 GPUs each. KServe runs `vllm serve … --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2`.
- If you set only TP=16 with 8 GPUs per pod, KServe internally rewrites it to TP=8 and PP=2.
- If the total GPUs fit in one pod (TP=8, PP=1), only the head pod is deployed.

This matches vLLM's own guidance: "set tensor_parallel_size to the number of GPUs per node and pipeline_parallel_size to the number of nodes". TP is best kept inside a node on fast interconnect, and PP goes across nodes. Source: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/serving/parallelism_scaling/

Restrictions in KServe 0.20:
- `TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE` and `PIPELINE_PARALLEL_SIZE` cannot be set via environment variables. Use `workerSpec`.
- It only works in Standard (non-Knative) mode.
- Autoscaling is not available, so the autoscaler class must be `none`.
- Storage must be a `pvc://` URI with ReadWriteMany access.
- There must be exactly one head pod.
- `PipelineParallelSize` is "not an autoscaling concept". It sets how many nodes run one model copy.
- Do not mix GPU types.

### `LLMInferenceService`

Source: https://kserve.github.io/website/docs/model-serving/generative-inference/llmisvc/llmisvc-configuration

```yaml
spec:
  parallelism:
    tensor: 4
    data: 8
    dataLocal: 4     # GPUs per node
    expert: true     # for MoE models
```

- The LeaderWorkerSet size is `data / dataLocal`.
